threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the tube' – locals know it's just 'the Overground' once you hit Clapton.
Caught the N68 last night and saw a guy arguing with the driver about a missing stop—turns out he was on the wrong bus all along.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw a guy juggling flaming torches on Richardplatz while a toddler inspected a stray cat. Only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you see a techno party break into a spontaneous street performance, with dancers and drum circles spilling onto the asphalt.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they can tell you the difference between a taco from La Taqueria and one from El Farolito, even in the dark.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus with a guy singing karaoke on his phone. He hit every note while the driver just rolled her eyes. Classic San Francisco moment.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think the Gràcia street parties are just for fun, but they often highlight local issues we face year-round that they overlook.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell they're new by the way they order 'café amb llet' and look confused when it arrives as a tiny cup instead of a mug.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the bus stop is where the bus actually arrives, not where you just stare at the countdown on your phone.
Caught the 133 last night, a guy serenaded the whole bus with a kazoo. Never knew it could be so lively at 2 AM in Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was really here when I saw a group of kids using a broken bench as a stage for their rap battle, effortlessly blending graffiti and laughter.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you find an abandoned factory turned into a wild flea market where DJs spin while you rummage through vintage clothes.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s from here if they still complain about the BART delays but use the 14 Mission as their main ride. It's a love-hate thing.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 14 Mission during a street fair—people spilling out like a can of sardines, smells of churros and empanadas mixing with the exhaust. Classic SF chaos.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists assume Gràcia is all bohemian cafes, but they miss the quiet plazas where locals argue over petanca instead of sipping on vermut.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell they're new when they still think La Rambla is a hidden gem instead of a tourist trap; the excitement in their eyes says it all.
